📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you need a side to go along with your main dinner entree and you need one fast, it's reassuring to know that shelf-stable, pantry-sitting canned goods have got your back. Included in Food Republic's list of inexpensive canned foods you'll use all the time are beans, and along with the plain black or red varieties (which typically need to be combined with other ingredients to make a reasonable side), you could also reach for scrumptious, creamy baked beans. But while they're totally fine heated up straight from the can, they can certainly benefit from a drizzle of molasses.

In a recent development, molasses might not be the first thing you think of when you consider add-ins, but many homemade recipes call for it, and for good reason. Made by boiling down sugarcane juice or refining sugar, the rich, thick syrup is slightly smoky and sweet, with robust, burnt caramel notes, making it a perfect match for deepening the flavor of sometimes weak-tasting canned baked beans and bringing them closer to homemade.

Sources indicate that it is for this reason that molasses is also preferable to honey here. Honey is intensely sweet, can taste almost floral at times, and has a delicate flavor, whereas molasses is bolder and has a meatier taste that can make its presence known among the other ingredients in the dish.

Sources indicate that it's important to note that there are three main types of molasses: light, dark, and blackstrap, and they each have different flavor profiles. For canned baked beans, you'll likely want to stick with light or dark because blackstrap is intensely bitter (also, light is the sweetest of the three, so if sweetness is important to you, go with that one). If you're heating the beans on the stove, you can start by drizzling in about half a tablespoon of molasses per 28-ounce can, bringing the mixture to a boil, and then simmering for about 10 minutes. If you're baking them, likewise, just stir in the molasses before putting the dish in the oven — it couldn't be simpler.

If you don't have any molasses sitting about, don't panic. There are plenty of other additions that can help upgrade canned baked beans and make them taste less, well, pantry-fied. Take brown sugar, for example — did you know that it's often just white sugar and molasses combined? A little bit will still bring that sweet contrast to balance out the savory flavors and give you a deeper, more complex finish.

Another great option is one you might normally use on your pancakes: maple syrup. You don't want to use the fake stuff that's primarily made of corn syrup and artificial flavors and colors, but rather 100% real Grade A maple syrup for the best flavor. Its sweetness again deliciously contrasts with and enhances the canned baked beans' savoriness, while the maple flavor adds its unique caramelly, toffee-like notes to the dish.

  • Think of Korean cuisine, and a sandwich likely isn't the first thing that comes to mind.
  • Easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

Think of Korean cuisine, and a sandwich likely isn't the first thing that comes to mind. However, bread-based dishes are widely enjoyed in the East Asian country, both in cafes and as street food. An especially popular breakfast rendition is gilgeori toast, a comforting breakfast sandwich stuffed with eggs and shredded vegetables.

Easy-to-make, packed with fiber, and delicious, the dish is a great candidate for your breakfast rotation. Traditionally, this sandwich calls for a fluffy loaf of milk or brioche bread, the buttery soft texture turning crisp on the outside once toasted. Meanwhile, the filling comprises a variable shredded vegetable medley: Cabbage traditionally forms the centerpiece, joined by carrots, onions, scallions, and often garlic chives. Mixed with egg and then pan-fried into an aesthetic golden-brown patty, the filling delectably complements the soft bread. Gilgeori is usually rounded out with a sprinkle of sugar and a drizzle of ketchup and mustard.

It's an assembly that easily comes together during bleary morning hours, yet nevertheless offers a nutritious start to the day. One sandwich can pack in around six ounces of shredded cabbage, which amounts to over 4 grams of fiber. Add up the fiber from a tablespoon of carrot, two of sliced onion, and two whole green onions, and you're including another 1.5 grams. Then, add in two slices of thick-cut brioche sandwich bread, and you've got an extra 2. That's about 7.5 grams, which is around a quarter of what you need a day, already knocked out by breakfast. Mixed with the roughly 6.5 grams of protein from the egg alongside filling bread, the sandwich serves as a terrific way to start the day.

Sources indicate that the morning isn't always the best time to precisely reconstruct a recipe. Thankfully, gilgeori toast welcomes a wide array of reinterpretations and ingredients. Starting with the bread, feel free to swap the milk bread for sourdough, whole wheat, or even a convenient store-bought whole grain like Ezekiel or Dave's Killer. You'll lose out on some of the dish's airiness, but potentially gain extra fiber content in the process. Two slices of Dave's Killer 21 Whole Grains and Seeds contain some 8 grams of fiber, more than doubling the total of the sandwich.

In a recent development, up the satiation further by adding on a slice of seared ham, a filling also enjoyed in Korea. And cheese is always welcome, whether American, cheddar, or fontina – Martha Stewart's go-to for breakfast sandwiches. Instead of the sugar sprinkle, lend the dish a sweet note by using jam: Raspberry or cherry jam makes a great fit. Not to mention, you can replace the ketchup and mustard with a condiment of your preference; you can buy a bottle of Gochujang Sriracha Hot Sauce online, for instance. The template of bread and shredded vegetables works with many flavors, perfect for morning enjoyment.

Not Cinnamon: Add A Pinch Of This Warm Spice To French Toast For A Flavor Boost

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Warm spices on French toast create a cozy, aromatic breakfast dish that warms your sinuses as much as your tongue.
  • Sources indicate that some folks call cardamom the queen of spices — and for good reason.
  • Six pods should yield about half a teaspoon of ground spice, enough for roughly six pieces of French toast (though pod sizes vary).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warm spices on French toast create a cozy, aromatic breakfast dish that warms your sinuses as much as your tongue. While traditional cinnamon is always a solid choice, cardamom French toast adds newly introduced layers of fresh, almost herbal notes for something far more complex and just as compatible with your other favorite seasonings.

Sources indicate that some folks call cardamom the queen of spices — and for good reason. As flavorful as it is versatile, it's a shelf-stable ingredient that lasts a long time, grinds easily into a powder, and seems to taste amazing with just about any sweet recipe you could think of. While it can be a tad on the expensive side, small amounts suffuse your French toast with deep flavor, so even a small jar of seeds can last you quite a while. The key is to mix it with your other dried spices to create a delicate flavor profile similar to mulled drinks, festive winter desserts, and spiced ciders.

Six pods should yield about half a teaspoon of ground spice, enough for roughly six pieces of French toast (though pod sizes vary). Since you want a smooth batter without much texture, it's best to grind the seeds into a fine powder before mixing. The moisture from eggs and milk should help protect the delicate spice, but remember that heat affects the flavor release of spices. Gently toasting the pods beforehand is a great way to bump up the flavor without using more of the pricey ingredient.

Though cardamom has quite a bit of flavor, it's also rather delicate and can slip into the background or be the star of the show, depending on your preferences. In sweet dishes, there are few warm spices it pairs poorly with, and more obscure ingredients can really elevate its flavor for something showstopping.

Just about any warming spice you'd associate with the colder months should pair beautifully with cardamom. Cinnamon is a bold counterpart that can carry most of the flavor profile without overshadowing it when used in moderation. Allspice and cloves are a match made in heaven, providing an almost berry-like warmth to counteract cardamom's cool, herbal notes. Ground or fresh ginger can add a touch of sharpness that offers quite a bit of contrast, providing a similar bite on the tongue to garlic that's far more compatible with sugary bases.

Recent findings suggest that if you really want to bump up the flavor of cardamom, don't stick to just spices. Floral notes from things like dried and ground orange peels, lychee, or guava really round out your French toast without overpowering your spices. These are highly compatible with cardamom and make your breakfast taste almost like a pomander, with an incredible bouquet of aromas the second your bread hits the pan. You can also use food-safe flavoring oils instead, mixing them into your wet ingredients for greater control over how much flavor you're adding.

There's probably no food more universally adored among Americans than pizza. Aside from being extremely customizable, every state has its own version of the best pizza — at least 15 distinct varieties and styles of making pizza can be found in the U.S. This makes it difficult to compare them. After all, the differences between a Detroit deep-dish and a chewy Latest Haven pie are many.

Sources indicate that this list sets aside nationwide pizza chains and restaurants that happen to have pizza on the menu, and seeks to highlight the most delicious pizza in each state. We considered customer reviews from all over the internet, as well as any regional or national honors attributed to each pizza, and compared the overall cultural legacy and impact of each restaurant. What we ended up with was delicious pizza places that were worthy of being the best in each state. When a good frozen pizza (or even the best frozen pizzas) won't cut it, these are the spots to check out.

It has been revealed that A well-traveled mainstay of Huntsville, Alabama, Valentina's Pizzeria has a reputation for serving Latest York-style pizza in a deep Southern atmosphere alongside other confections and dishes made in an Italian-American tradition. Joe Carlucci, the maestro behind Valentina's Pizzeria, is a co-founder of the World Pizza Champions organization, and his pizzeria is a local favorite — just check the comments on any of Valentina's Pizzeria's posts.

25783 Huntsville Brownsferry Rd, Madison, AL 35756.

It has been revealed that people love Moose's Tooth Pub & Pizzeria because it delivers on its goal of offering a "gourmet pizza experience, focusing on creative, quality food in a casual environment." The menu (with a robust list of temporary featured pizzas) reflects a creative urge to innovate. Moose's Tooth is the best-reviewed pizza in Alaska, according to Yelp and Google. There's no shortage of outdoor ambience in Alaska, so in addition to its indoor pub seating, Moose's Tooth offers outdoor, fireside seating for crisp days and nights.

3300 Old Seward Hwy, Anchorage, AK 99503.

It has been revealed that every pie at Via Della Slice Shop is crafted with artful attention to detail, and it's this skill and the friendly customer service that keep people coming back for more. Though a small and relatively simple operation, the restaurant is dedicated to making pizza of the highest quality; it proofs its dough for at least two days. According to Yelp, the vodka pizza is a particular favorite among returning customers, but Via Della is noted for its rotating flavors.

222 N 5th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85003.

While DeLuca's Pizza has recently received accolades for its unconventional Spite Burger, it is best known for its brick-oven-baked pizza pies sold out of two locations in Hot Springs, Arkansas. Pizza influencer Dave Portnoy gave DeLuca's pizza an 8.7 out of 10, adding that it "blew [his] socks off [and] can compete with anybody in the country." And the non-influencers love it, too, with some people even driving multiple hours just to get a bite.

Sources indicate that tony's Pizza Napoletana was recognized this year as the No. 5 best pizzeria in the world, according to 50 Top Pizza. Tony's is just as popular with customers as with critics, as it's maintained a high star rating through tens of thousands of eviews on Google. Tony Gemigani — owner and 13-time World Pizza Champion — has spent years perfecting his pies; any West Coast pizza crawl would be incomplete without a visit to Tony's.

1570 Stockton St, San Francisco, CA 94133.

Blue Pan Pizza offers delicious, Detroit-style pizza with a little bit of Denver flair. It's known for its Detroit-style pies, but it offers other versions and has been noted by folks for its tasty gluten-free options as well.

In a recent development, detroit-style pizza is pan-baked pizza, and Blue Pan even serves to-go pies in rectangular, bright blue boxes made to look like its titular bakeware. Blue Pan was voted Readers' Choice for Best Denver Pizzeria by Denver Westword in 2024 and enjoys a huge local following.

Recent findings suggest that A staple of Connecticut and specifically Latest Haven-style pizza since 1938, Sally's Apizza is a legendary spot amongst locals and pizza fanatics. New Haven-style pizza is made of high-hydration dough and cooked at a high heat in order to achieve a chewy, airy crust.

A fresh fan of Sally's wrote on Yelp, "It was a perfect meal, in a nice, cozy old school spot, that I'll definitely be craving until I'm back in town.".

237 Wooster St, Upcoming Haven, CT 06511.

La Pizzeria Metro is a lovely little pizza place with two Delaware locations that offer a breezy, friendly dining experience and delicious pizza. Customers can even settle at the bar and tables with a view of pizza chefs at work.

La Pizzeria Metro's many specialty pizzas are named after landmark spots in Wilmington, an apt choice given how popular the place is with locals. One local reviewer wrote, "La Pizzeria Metro absolutely nails [creative pizza]. Their pizzas somehow manage to feel both authentic and wildly inventive.".

It's no secret online that Florida's pizza options leave much to be desired. But Satchel's Pizza in Gainesville is a diamond in the rough.

Industry observers note that it's a beloved destination for locals who praise both its delicious pizza and eclectic atmosphere. Some would even argue it's not just the best pizza in Florida; it might just be the best in the south. Even with thousands of reviews online, Satchel's maintains a very high star average rating.

1800 NE 23rd Ave, Gainesville, FL 32609.

Antico Pizza Napoletana is a pizzeria located in Atlanta's Little Italia. Founded by Giovanni "Gio" Di Palma, Antico offers only Neapolitan-style pizza cooked in wood-burning ovens, and thanks to its impeccable quality, earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2023. The pizza is so good, in fact, that it earned the highest score out of all pizzerias reviewed in Zagat's first survey of pizza places in major U.S. cities.

Though Pizza Mamo only began selling pies in 2020, it's rapidly been established as a neighborhood mainstay in Honolulu and has earned an Ilima Award — Hawaii's most prestigious restaurant recognition. Pizza Mamo's pies are based on a four-day fermented dough that provides a satisfying, chewy consistency in every slice. A local Yelp reviewer wrote, "Best pizza I've had on the island ... the pepperoni has a nice spice to it, and the dough is PERFECT.".

16 N Hotel St, Honolulu, HI 96817.

Despite its remote location, Embers by the Lake has garnered tons of glowing online reviews – and the pizzeria's gorgeous lakeside backdrop is only a small part of what customers love. A great spot for family outings, Embers by the Lake has earned official recognition determined by customers, entities, and critics, including a local organization called North Idaho Life, which awarded it the first 5-Star Dining Destination Award.

12008 N Woodland Beach Dr, Hauser, ID 83854.

Recent findings suggest that vito and Nick's Pizzeria is known for its Chicago tavern-style pies, which are made with a round, cracker-thin crust and cut into squares. It's a parlor that's been in business for more than 75 years and is an iconic institution to locals and tourists alike. The CBS Chicago Pizza Tournament awarded Vito and Nick's the grand prize in 2023, and the parlor has been positively featured on Food Network's "Diners, Drive-ins and Dives.".

Recent findings suggest that tre Mori is much more than a pizza restaurant — the menu offers finely crafted pasta dishes and baked breads — but the pizza is definitely its signature. Dedicated to an old-style Italian sensibility, Tre Mori utilizes fresh and home-prepared ingredients, as well as supplies and foods imported from Italy (including the beautiful brick oven). On Yelp, Tre Mori is a top-100 US pizza joint, and on Onebite, it earns consistently positive reviews from customers.

8220 E 106th St Suite 200, Indianapolis, IN 46256.

Recent findings suggest that fong's Pizza in Des Moines occupies the same space that once housed the oldest Chinese restaurant in America. As such, it offers a fusion of Chinese flavors and Italian fundamentals. Fong's claims to be the originator of the crab rangoon pizza (Alton Brown swears by it), and the restaurant earns great customer feedback for its fresh ingredients and timely service.

317 E Court Ave, Des Moines, IA 50309.

According to recent reports, even though Back Alley Pizza has only been operating for a little over 10 years, it has become a staple of Newton, Kansas, and a magnet for regional recognition. On Yelp, satisfied customers rejoice over the best pizza they've ever had, period. Though Back Alley Pizza doesn't claim a signature "style" of pizza, it does tout its original BBQ pizza as a signature. But you'll be happy with any slice you try.

Miguel's Pizza feels like a well-loved small business with a dedicated following and a commitment to capturing Kentucky's rustic charm in combination with a warm, friendly atmosphere. Pizza Today has featured Miguel's as a must-stop destination, and many recognize the pizzeria as a key element in the economic development of Kentucky's Red River Gorge. All of that is because of the quality of the pizza, which people just can't get enough of.

1890 Natural Bridge Rd, Slade, KY 40376.

Industry observers note that zander White, founder of Zee's Pizzeria, pursued pizza-making as a hobby until the COVID-19 pandemic, during which he had to find a latest way to support his family. White was so successful selling pies from his kitchen that he opened Zee's Pizzeria, which was named one of the top pizza places in New Orleans by Gambit Weekly. Customers appreciate the thin crust, sweet sauce, and classic taste.

3914 Baronne St, Upcoming Orleans, LA 70115.

The purveyors at Brickyard Hollow Brewing Tech giant (which began in Yarmouth) realized that few things pair better with a glass of craft beer than a slice of craft pizza, which has become as much of a draw as the beer – if not more so.

Brickyard Hollow has a greater mission to provide fun and comfort to local Maine communities and residents looking to connect more closely with their neighbors. It's received rave reviews from local critics and is rapidly expanding thanks to overwhelming regional support.

In December 2024, Barstool pizza reviewer Dave Portnoy stopped by TinyBrickOven to do a quick slice review. He gave TinyBrickOven's pizza a 7.9/10 rating and $60,000 to turn the small business major. It was that good. TinyBrickOven is a staple of Baltimore, with local customers and other supporters even accepting the owner's self-anointed title, "the Michael Jordan of pizza.".

1036 Light St, Baltimore, MD 21230.

In a recent development, widely regarded as Boston's oldest operating pizza place, Regina Pizzeria has been serving slices and pies around Boston's North End since 1926. The quality comes from an impeccable dough — chewy yet crisp and perfectly charred — that's baked inside a 900-degree gas-fired oven. Boston Magazine calls it one of the city's best, and in 2018, Tripadvisor named Regina Pizzeria the best in the nation. Taste of Massachusetts included it in its list of top 11 favorite pizzas in the state.

Industry observers note that in 2024, Yelp named Loui's Pizza in Hazel Park, Michigan, as the best pizza spot in the Midwest. It's been family-owned since 1977, and for nearly half a century, it's been pumping out top-tier Detroit-style pies that are chewy, crisp, cheesy, and properly sauced. The Detroit Metro Times ranked Loui's as the No. 1 Detroit-style pizza in the area, citing its "tangy sauce, crispy caramelized edges, and an abundance of cheese" as a few of the reasons why this pizza stands out.

23141 Dequindre Rd, Hazel Park, MI 48030.

When you have the endorsement from global food aficionado Andrew Zimmern, you know you're doing something right. Punch Pizza is the people's pizzeria, a beloved St. Paul institution that has now expanded to 12 locations. It specializes in Neapolitan-style pizza, cooked for about a minute and a half in a scorching-hot, wood-burning oven. It has earned numerous awards and recognitions, including a Quality Business Award in 2025.

Leña Pizza + Bagels is giving Mississippi some long-deserved culinary attention. Chef and owner Marisol Doyle grew up in Mexico, moved to Mississippi, and studied pizza making in Naples, Italy. The restaurant was quickly named one of the best in the United States by both the Newly introduced York Times and the prestigious Italian pizza review board, 50 Top Pizza. However, the biggest honor came in 2024, when Doyle was named one of the top 100 pizza chefs in the world.

331 Cotton Row, Cleveland, MS 38732.

You've heard of New York-, New Haven-, and Detroit-style pizza, but — unless you're from Missouri, you probably aren't familiar with St. Louis-style pies. And Pirrone's Pizzeria, which has been around since 1976, arguably makes the best one in the state. The rectangular dough is crisp and cracker-thin and covered in melted Provel, a triple-blend processed cheese invented in St. Louis.

1775 Washington St, Florissant, MO 63033.

Eugene's Pizza has remained a community staple for over 60 years. In 2015 and 2016, it was the back-to-back champion of the Montana Mint pizza bracket, and in 2026, Reader's Digest recognized the pizzeria as the best in Montana. Eugene's serves some wild pies, with topping options ranging from taco-seasoned ground beef and sauerkraut to shrimp and mandarin oranges.

193 Klein Ave, Glasgow, MT 59230.

Founded in 1919 by World War I veteran Alfonso Orsi, the bakery and pizzeria has racked up thousands of excellent reviews on Google. Its near-perfect score has a lot to do with its pizza dough — prepared fresh in small batches every morning using a simple recipe of yeast, salt, water, and high-gluten wheat flour. Tripadvisor ranks it the top pizzeria in Omaha, and our sister site, Mashed, listed it as the best Italian restaurant in Nebraska.

621 Pacific St, Omaha, NE 68108.

Sources indicate that red Dwarf is a triumvirate of pleasures: it's a pizzeria, rum-infused Tiki party, and rock show all in one. The Detroit-style pies have a "crispy edge [and an] airy center" and are loaded with topping combinations that include everything from brown sugar-glazed ham, pineapple, and jalapeño to mushrooms, peppers, and garlic creme sauce. In 2025, Red Dwarf won the Reader's Choice Best Pizza Award from Las Vegas Weekly, and commenters on Facebook, Reddit, and Google agree it's the best pizza in town.

1305 Vegas Valley Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89169.

In New England, New Haven-style pizza gets all the attention, but venture a few hundred miles north, and you'll find another popular regional variety: Greek-style. With these pies, the dough bakes in a high-walled pan that's generously coated with olive oil to achieve an extra-crisp, almost fried bottom crust. And few places execute it better than New Hampshire's Tilton House of Pizza. It appears on roundups as the best pizza place in New Hampshire and has a near-perfect rating on Google.

New Jersey certainly takes its pizza seriously. Part of that reputation can be attributed to the De Lorenzo family, who opened their first New Jersey restaurant in 1936. In 2021, Food and Wine recognized New Jersey as the best state for pizza in the country, calling out De Lorenzo's specifically as "one of the finest classic pies in the entire Northeast." Its namesake tomato pie is hand-stretched, layered with cheese — then sauce — and baked until charred.

According to the Albuquerque Journal, Pizza Barn is slinging some of the best pies in all of Newly introduced Mexico. And any pizzeria with a fireplace and a drive-thru deserves special recognition. Pizza Barn is known for its roasted green chiles — a popular condiment throughout the state — which it liberally scatters over its pies and breadsticks.

11 Plaza Loop, Edgewood, NM 87015.

Recent findings suggest that john's of Bleecker, the famed no-slice pizzeria, has been blazing dough in its coal-fired oven since 1929. The pies are thin, crisp, and beautifully blistered, topped with a just-sweet-enough tomato sauce, and then baked fast and hot. With Google reviewers praising its old-school traditions, service, and the pizza itself, this is one of the most respected Fresh York City pizzerias — if not the world.

278 Bleecker St, Newly introduced York, NY 10014.

Industry observers note that oakwood Pizza Box anchors the pizza scene in the North Carolina Research Triangle. It was awarded Best Pizza in 2026 by Midtown Magazine, a publication that highlights life in the greater Raleigh area. It serves an excellent Northeastern-style pizza: thin, foldable, cheesy, and not overly sauced. Its square pies are about the size of a large pillowcase and can be ordered with a sesame seed crust.

North Dakota has carved out its own style of pizza, which is heartier than your average Neapolitan pie or Fresh York-style slice. Since the early 2000s, Rhombus Guys have been baking doughy, tire-sized pizzas that have earned it the reputation as one of the best (and most inventive) pizzerias in the state. The restaurant's signature T-Rex pizza — a hulking combination of pepperoni, sausage, and other toppings — won the Grand Forks People's Choice competition six years in a row.

Rarely do you see such a consensus on Reddit and Facebook, but when it comes to Il Rione, almost everyone agrees that it makes one of the best pies in Cleveland — if not the state. It serves a gorgeous Newly introduced York-style pizza that, in 2025, beat out 32 other pizzerias to win the title of Best Pizza in the Land from the local media outlet I'm From Cleveland. It's also a favorite of Iron Chef (and Cleveland native) Michael Symon.

1303 W 65th St, Cleveland, OH 44102.

Recent findings suggest that most of the pizzerias on this list are primarily standalone restaurants. Hideaway is one of the few exceptions, with 27 locations across three states. In 1957, its original location opened in Stillwater, next to the Oklahoma State University campus. With pizza names like Pepperonipalooza and Aporkalypse, it's no surprise that The Fresh York Times listed it as one of 15 of its readers' favorite pizza places from around the world.

Recent findings suggest that at Lovely's Fifty Fifty,  chef/co-owner Sarah Minnick uses her art degree to craft her stunning edible mosaics. Her sourdough starter, local grains, flowers, and seasonal ingredients help her pizza achieve an inimitable tang and toothsome chew. With write-ups in Portland Monthly, a feature in Food & Wine, and an impressive 9.0 score from the Infatuation, Lovely's has become one of the most respected pizzerias in the country.

4039 N Mississippi Ave, Portland, OR 97217.

Opened in 1924, the Corropolese Italian Bakery & Deli is most famous for its tomato pie: a sturdy, cake-like dough covered in smooth tomato sauce, sprinkled with a light dusting of Romano cheese, and served at room temperature. Over the century, it has become a cornerstone of Philadelphia food culture, so much so that in 2023, Corropolese's won Herr's second annual #FlavoredbyPhilly contest. The prize? A Herr's chip flavor inspired by its famous tomato pie.

For such a tiny state, Rhode Island has plenty of quality pizzerias, but one that keeps showing up on lists of local favorites is Pasquale's. With a treasured Associazione Vera Pizza Napoletana certification, it's no surprise the pizzeria has earned so many accolades. In 2025, 50 Top Pizza named it the 12th best in the U.S., and Rhode Island Monthly magazine acknowledges it as one of the state's great pizzerias.

59 S County Commons Way, Wakefield, RI 02879.

In a recent development, D'Allesandro's Pizza has been making its hand-tossed pizzas since 2006. In 2021, Big Seven Travel named the pizzeria No. 1 in South Carolina. Four years later, D'Allesandro's was one of three pizzerias to win the title of Best Pizza Joint from The Guide to South Carolina. Eater followed suit in 2025, featuring D'Alessandro's on its list of the 13 best stops for pizza in Charleston.

Opened in 1959, Charlie's Pizza House is the oldest pizzeria in South Dakota. Its lineup of eclectic specialty pizzas, with names like "Hepburn's Spicy Delight," "John Wayne's BBQ Style," and "Marilyn's Mermaid Heaven," which is topped with shrimp, crab, and green and black olives, honors Hollywood stars of past decades. The restaurant has also received national acclaim, with the Food Network naming Charlie's South Dakota's best pizza place.

Recent findings suggest that A Dopo is a wood-fired pizzeria in downtown Knoxville that has won over the hearts of residents and college students with its sourdough Neapolitan-style pizzas. The dinner-only pizzeria stepped into the national spotlight after making the list of USA Today's 2025 Restaurants of the Year, and it continues to rack up recognition, most recently receiving a nod from the Michelin Guide in 2026.

516 Williams St, Knoxville, TN 37917.

Industry observers note that cane Rosso is a pizzeria that has blossomed into nine locations across Texas. Its wood-fired pizzas are all 14 inches and baked in a blazing-hot oven, giving each pie its "signature leopard-spotted crust." Its toppings — beef brisket, bacon marmalade, smoked mozzarella, habanero honey — have a distinct Texas flair. In 2021, Food & Wine named it one of the best pizzerias in Texas, and it has since maintained its reputation for excellence.

It has been revealed that the Pie Underground's flagship location, open since 1980, is the most beloved of its dozens of locations — just a stone's throw from the University of Utah campus. Unsurprisingly, its menu reads like it was conceived by the hungry college kids who still love the place, featuring bold concoctions like the "Bacon-Berry Pie," a pizza topped with chicken, bacon, feta, and a strawberry balsamic sauce.

Folino's embodies the ethos of pizza artistry. Its naturally leavened dough uses a 14- year-old starter culture and is cold-proofed for three days to achieve a one-of-a-kind crust that's light, layered, and intentionally tangy. It has expanded to multiple locations throughout Vermont, and it's consistently won Best Pizza Restaurant from Seven Days, an independent weekly newspaper covering Vermont news, politics, food, and culture.

Dr. Ho's describes itself as "the alternative pizza." And we can't help but agree. The pies, each made with hand-tossed dough, include an impressive configuration of toppings like the buffalo chicken with pineapple and pickled jalapeño peppers or the shrimp with homemade basil pesto. Its commitment to innovative combinations, quality ingredients, and sheer quantity makes this one a favorite among Virginians.

4916 Plank Rd, North Garden, VA 22959.

Industry observers note that the Carlson Block is a destination restaurant, nestled cozily in Wilkeson, a tiny coal-mining town. The Seattle Times featured the pizzeria, asking rhetorically if it's making the best pizza in the state. The pies, pulled charred from the wood-fired oven, glow like an oil painting encased in a rich wooden frame. House-made mozzarella, seasonal ingredients, a deft hand, and a commitment to the craft ensure Carlson Block will remain among the state's best pizza places.

531 Church St, Wilkeson, WA 98396.

According to recent reports, you know what you're getting at Pies & Pints: quality draft beer and fiercely innovative pizzas. Seriously, the pie lineup is extraordinary, with topping combinations like grapes and Gorgonzola, Sriracha shrimp, and Cuban pork with fresh pineapple, jalapeños, and crème fraiche. It's an endless list, which means you'll just have to come back again and again to try them all, as many West Virginia residents have been doing.

In a recent development, open for over a century, Wells Brothers serves a handful of Italian classics, but it's most famous for its pizzas. In 2026, The Journal Times awarded Wells Brothers the title of Best Pizza and Best Italian Restaurant. The restaurant has amassed thousands of glowing Google reviews, indicating that it may keep serving its beautifully-charred, square-cut pies well into the next century.

A relative newcomer, Bella Fuoco is wowing with its blistered, wood-fired pizzas. The concept started as a food truck, but its brick-and-mortar location has helped chef-owner Brenna Kosowicz bring her pizza to even more hungry Wyomingites. In 2025, Bella Fuoco was formally recognized when the Wyoming Tribune Eagle awarded it Best of the Best in the pizza category.

2115 Warren Ave, Cheyenne, WY 82001.

Determining the "best" pizza is largely subjective. For states with a distinct regional variation, we selected shops that are an excellent representation of that style. We also considered restaurants that have stood the test of time or are pillars of the community, and placed weight on glowing social media reviews and awards. Overall customer experience was also considered, as was the impact on the home state's pizza culture.

How to Start a Side Business While Working Full-Time

📅 19 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2259 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Choosefi

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that what's your FI number?
  • Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.
  • According to recent reports, the number one reason side businesses fail is not lack of funding, bad timing, or tough competition — it is building something nobody wants to buy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that what's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds.

The one number that changes everything.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

According to recent reports, the number one reason side businesses fail is not lack of funding, bad timing, or tough competition — it is building something nobody wants to buy. Before you spend a dollar on a website, business cards, or inventory, you need to validate that real people will pay real money for what you are offering.

Validation does not require a perfect product. It requires proof of demand. Talk to 10 people who match your target customer. Describe what you blueprint to offer. Ask two questions: "Would you pay for this?" and "How much would you pay?" If 3 or more say yes with a specific dollar amount, you have a viable idea. If most say "that sounds cool" but hesitate on paying, you have a hobby.

It has been revealed that the FI community has a particular advantage here. Many FI seekers have already cut their expenses to the point where a side business does not need to generate massive revenue to make a meaningful impact. Even $500 to $1,000 per month in side business income — invested consistently — can shave years off your FI timeline.

According to recent reports, forget building a $1 million business. Your only goal is reaching $1,000 in total revenue as quickly as possible. That first $1,000 proves three things: people will pay you, you can deliver, and the business model works. Everything after $1,000 is optimization. The FI community calls this the "ramen profitable" stage — your business covers its own costs and generates even a small surplus. From there, you compound both your skills and your revenue.

Side business income is the ultimate FI accelerator because it attacks both sides of the equation. Your day job covers expenses while 100% of your side income goes directly to investments. If your side business generates $1,500 per month and you invest all of it at 7% annual returns, you will have over $450,000 in 15 years. That is not a theoretical number — that is the real math of why thousands of FI seekers build side businesses.

One of the first decisions you face is how to structure your business legally. For most side businesses, the choice is between operating as a sole proprietorship (the default — no paperwork needed) or forming an LLC (Limited Liability Tech giant). Here is the honest comparison.

A sole proprietorship is what you are by default when you start earning money on the side. There is no registration required at the federal level (though you may need a local business license). The income flows directly to your personal tax return on Schedule C. The downside: your personal assets — savings, home equity, investments — are not separated from business liabilities.

An LLC creates a legal separation between you and your business. If someone sues your business, your personal assets are generally protected. Formation costs range from $50 (states like Kentucky and Colorado) to $500 (California charges $800 per year just for the privilege of having an LLC). For most side businesses, an LLC is worth forming once you have paying customers.

Side business income is taxed differently than your W-2 paycheck, and the surprises can be painful if you are not prepared.

In a recent development, self-employment tax: You pay both the employee AND employer portions of Social Security and Medicare — a combined 15.3% on top of your income tax. On W-2 income, your employer covers half. On side business income, you cover it all.

Industry observers note that quarterly estimated taxes: The IRS expects you to pay taxes as you earn, not once a year in April. If you owe more than $1,000 in taxes from side business income, you need to file quarterly estimated payments (Form 1040-ES) by April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.

Sources indicate that deductions that reduce your tax bill: Home office (simplified method: $5/sq ft up to 300 sq ft = $1,500 deduction), internet (business percentage), equipment, software subscriptions, mileage ($0.76 per mile in 2027), health insurance premiums (if self-employed), and retirement contributions (Solo 401k allows up to $75,000/year). These deductions are a significant FI advantage because they reduce both income tax AND self-employment tax.

It has been revealed that ready to unlock a world of free travel? Start with the Chase Sapphire Preferred® Card.

$95 annual fee | Earn 75,000 bonus points.

Side hustlers! With the Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card you can earn free travel from your business expenses.

$95 annual fee | Earn 100,000 bonus points.

The Capital One Venture Rewards Credit Card can be used to offset almost any travel expense.

Industry observers note that chooseFI has partnered with CardRatings for our coverage of credit card products. ChooseFI and CardRatings may receive a commission from card issuers.

The biggest constraint for side business owners is not money — it is time. You have 168 hours per week. Your day job takes 40-50. Sleep takes 49-56. That leaves 62-79 hours for everything else: family, health, friends, and your business. The key is not finding more time. It is being ruthlessly strategic about the time you have.

Industry observers note that the 5-5-2 Framework: Dedicate 5 hours per weeknight (after work), 5 hours on Saturday, and 2 hours on Sunday to your business during the launch phase. That is 12 hours per week — enough to build meaningful momentum without destroying your health or relationships. After launch, you can often reduce to 5-8 hours per week for maintenance.

Batch your work. Do not context-switch between your day job and side business throughout the day. Dedicate specific blocks of time to specific tasks: Monday and Wednesday evenings for content creation, Tuesday and Thursday for customer communication, Saturday morning for strategic work.

The FI community offers a unique perspective on this question. Traditional business advice says to go full-time when your side income replaces your salary. The FI approach is more nuanced: your side business does not need to replace your income if your investments are covering the gap.

Consider going full-time when your side business income covers at least 75% of your essential expenses for 6 consecutive months, you have 12 months of expenses in cash reserves, your business is growing (not plateauing), and you have health insurance figured out independently of your employer.

But here is the FI twist: many people in the community deliberately keep their side business as a side business forever. A day job provides steady income, benefits, and 401(k) matching, while the side business provides additional investment capital. This "two-income engine" approach can cut your FI timeline dramatically. If your day job covers all expenses and your side business generates $2,000 per month in investable income, you add over $700,000 to your portfolio in 15 years at 7% returns.

The decision depends on your personal FI strategy. Some people want to build a business that replaces their job and provides fulfillment in early retirement. Others want to maximize total income during their accumulation phase and retire from everything. Both are valid paths — the vital thing is making the choice intentionally with the math in front of you.

From idea to first dollar with minimal risk.

Talk to 10 people who match your target customer profile. Describe your offer and ask if they would pay, and how much. Get at least 3 verbal commitments before building anything. If you cannot find 3 out of 10, pivot your idea.

Pro tip: Pre-sell before you build. Create a simple landing page describing your product or service and see if people will put down a deposit or join a waitlist.

Recent findings suggest that open a separate business bank account (free at most banks). File for an LLC in your state if you are ready for revenue. Get an EIN from the IRS (free, takes 5 minutes online). Set aside 30% of every dollar earned for taxes.

Pro tip: Do not commingle business and personal finances. A separate bank account makes tax time dramatically easier and protects your LLC liability shield.

Recent findings suggest that create the simplest version of your product or service that delivers value. A consultant needs a one-page website and a Calendly link. A product business needs one SKU, not twenty. A freelancer needs a portfolio with three examples. Launch ugly and improve based on real customer feedback.

Pro tip: Spend less than $200 on your MVP. If you need to spend more, you are overbuilding before you have proven demand.

Sources indicate that your first customers will come from your personal network, not from marketing. Tell everyone you know what you are building. Offer a founding-member discount in exchange for detailed feedback and a testimonial. The goal is revenue and learning, not profit.

Pro tip: Ask every customer two questions after delivery: "What was the best part?" and "What would you change?" These answers shape your product roadmap.

Once you have proven the model works, build systems so the business runs efficiently. Create templates, automate invoicing, document your processes. Find the acquisition channel that produces the best customers (referrals, content marketing, paid ads) and double down on it.

It has been revealed that pro tip: Track your effective hourly rate. If you earn $1,000 in a month and spend 20 hours, your rate is $50/hour. If you spend 80 hours, it is $12.50/hour — below minimum wage. Optimize for $/hour, not just total revenue.

In a recent development, the most powerful FI strategy is not choosing between your day job and a side business — it is running both simultaneously. Your day job covers all living expenses, employer benefits, and 401(k) matching. Your side business generates pure investment capital. If your side business produces $2,000 per month and you invest every dollar at 7% annual returns, you add over $700,000 to your portfolio in 15 years. That is the difference between retiring at 55 and retiring at 45.

Check your employment contract and organization handbook for non-compete clauses, moonlighting policies, and intellectual property agreements. Many employers have no policy against side businesses as long as they do not compete, use company resources, or interfere with your job performance. If your contract has restrictions, consult an employment attorney before launching. Transparency is usually the safest approach if your side business is in a completely different industry.

Most service-based side businesses can launch for under $200: a domain name ($12/year), basic website hosting ($5-$15/month), and a business bank account (free). Product businesses may need $500-$2,000 for initial inventory. The FI approach is to minimize upfront investment and validate before spending. If your idea requires $10,000+ to test, consider whether there is a simpler version you can launch first.

Businesses with flexible hours and no geographic constraints work best: freelance writing, web development, consulting in your area of expertise, online tutoring, bookkeeping, virtual assistance, and digital product creation (courses, templates, ebooks). The key criteria are: work can be done on your schedule, no physical storefront needed, and revenue can grow without proportional time investment.

It has been revealed that report all income on Schedule C of your personal tax return. Pay self-employment tax (15.3%) plus income tax on profits. File quarterly estimated taxes using Form 1040-ES if you expect to owe $1,000 or more. Deduct legitimate business expenses: home office, internet (business %), equipment, software, mileage, and health insurance premiums. Consider a Solo 401(k) to shelter up to $75,000/year from taxes — this is one of the most powerful FI tools available to self-employed individuals.

Start as a sole proprietor during the validation phase (no cost, no paperwork). Form an LLC once you have paying customers and revenue. An LLC protects your personal assets (home, savings, investments) from business lawsuits and debts. Formation costs range from $50-$500 depending on your state. California charges $800/year minimum, which may not be worth it until you are earning at least $10,000/year from the business.

In a recent development, dramatically. If your day job covers all expenses at a 50% savings rate, you reach FI in about 17 years. Add $2,000/month in side business income invested entirely, and your effective savings rate jumps well above 60% — cutting your FI timeline to roughly 12-13 years. At $3,000/month side income, you could reach FI in under 10 years from starting. The key insight: side business income has nearly 100% savings rate because your day job already covers expenses.

According to recent reports, starting a side business while working full-time is one of the most powerful financial moves you can make on the path to FI. Validate your idea before spending money, set up basic legal and tax infrastructure, launch an MVP quickly, and focus relentlessly on reaching your first $1,000 in revenue. The beauty of the side business approach is that your day job covers all expenses while your business income goes directly toward building wealth. Even modest side income of $1,000 to $2,000 per month, invested consistently over 10-15 years, can add hundreds of thousands of dollars to your portfolio and cut years off your timeline to financial independence.

Breaking: Make A Reuben Upside Down-Style For More Caramelized Flavor

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The origins of the Reuben are disputed, with some saying that it was invented in Nebraska while others insist that it is a Latest York original. Regardless of where you think this iconic sandwich was born, the combination of corned beef, cheese, sauerkraut, and Russian dressing (or Thousand Island dressing) on rye bread is something that few people mess with. The method for making it also tends to remain unchanged, with many restaurants and home cooks pressing it in a sandwich press or skillet. This is just fine for the traditional recipe, but if you want to give your Reuben a layer of caramelized flavor, you're going to need to shake up tradition just a little bit by making it upside down-style. Instead of building your sandwich starting with the bread, start with the cheese touching the pan or baking sheet.

Cheeses like Swiss, which is the preferred kind for making a classic Reuben sandwich recipe, contain proteins and a little bit of sugar in the form of lactose. It's these two elements that react to the direct heat of the pan to create the Maillard reaction, which is when food gets browned, developing complex flavors that make it irresistibly delicious. This contributes to a caramelized note in your sandwich and echoes the toasty notes of the bread. By adding additional cheese between the layers of meat, you ensure that there is a melty element as well. Adding the kraut right before assembling the final product prevents the moisture from getting in the way of browning.

Recent findings suggest that since the cheese is coming into direct contact with the cooking surface, you're going to need to ensure that it doesn't stick to whatever you're using to make your sandwich. If you're opting to make your Reuben on the stovetop, you're going to want to use a nonstick pan. Make sure it's hot, too, as this can also help prevent food from sticking. You're also going to want to use a thin, wide spatula that you can easily slide between the cheese and the pan to flip your sandwich halves so that you can toast the bread.

If you're choosing to bake your Reuben upside down-style, be sure to use Ina Garten's favorite thing to line a sheet pan: parchment paper, which you can easily peel away from the toasted cheese after flipping your sandwich halves over. You'll also want to ensure you're baking your sandwiches at the right temperature to get both the cheese and bread toasted and crisp, and 375 degrees Fahrenheit is typically ideal.

Regardless of which method you choose, you should always spread some kind of fat on your bread for even more flavor, and this is something you can play around with without breaking from tradition too much. Butter or mayonnaise are typically used in toasted sandwiches, but you can also opt for ghee, which has a nuttier flavor. Bacon fat is also an intensely flavorful alternative, but if you want to mirror the meatiness of the corned beef, go for beef tallow.

#229727. What Does Gen Z Think About Political Polarization?

What Does Gen Z Think About Political Polarization?

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1255 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Berkeley

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Polarization is a fact of political life in the U.S.
  • “Polarization doesn’t seem to be a fixed trend in Gen Z’s minds,” mentioned Jadon Urogdy.
  • Urogdy and his classmates also found that Gen Z, which is the cohort born between 1997 and 2012 and considered the first true “digital natives,” is more comfortable than their elders in having a political conversation online—findings that suggest they may be more reachable and receptive to online interventions aimed at reducing polarization.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Polarization is a fact of political life in the U.S. today. Gen Z, however, is less inclined than older generations to view it as a permanent fixture in American politics, according to research by students in the Stanford political science course Democracy in the Balance: Polarization and the Road Ahead. Students found that Gen Z is more optimistic than any other age group about the possibility of bridging the political divide in America.

“Polarization doesn’t seem to be a fixed trend in Gen Z’s minds,” mentioned Jadon Urogdy. “We have a bright future. Our identities and views are still malleable, and that’s exactly why this moment matters so much.”.

Urogdy and his classmates also found that Gen Z, which is the cohort born between 1997 and 2012 and considered the first true “digital natives,” is more comfortable than their elders in having a political conversation online—findings that suggest they may be more reachable and receptive to online interventions aimed at reducing polarization.

Urogdy’s results were among many findings from Democracy in the Balance: Polarization and the Road Ahead, a spring quarter course taught by Ashley Fabrizio, a Stanford alum and head of research at the nonpartisan think tank More in Common. Working with Fabrizio and her team, students created and conducted a nationally representative survey of 1,610 U.S. adults that oversampled Gen Z to provide a more granular look into their political attitudes and opinions.

Industry observers note that fabrizio, who has taught the course for three years, has found that working with students surfaces concerns that standard polling may miss. “If we want to know what Gen Z’s political beliefs and attitudes are, we should let our students, as members of Gen Z, use their intuition to decide what matters in a survey,” Fabrizio explained.

According to recent reports, working in small groups, students were allocated several minutes of survey time to explore topics such as the political influence of online content promoting masculinity—aka the “manosphere”—the religious revival in Gen Z’s lives, and their beliefs about the American dream. Fabrizio guided students step by step through survey design, showing them how to craft research questions, field the survey, analyze data, and, finally, present their findings.

Students also examined the academic literature on polarization’s effects in American politics, such as how it contributes to political gridlock, drives support for political violence, and erodes trust in American institutions.

According to recent reports, “There are many legitimate divisions in politics over competing policies and values, but polarization often drives us apart unnecessarily,” said Fabrizio. “Young Americans will have to find their own ways of bridging partisan differences and overcoming misconceptions about one another. I hope this class helps students see the value of doing so and gives them a sense of agency in addressing polarization.”.

Sources indicate that natalia Galperin was excited about the opportunity to run her own study from start to finish, a first for the Stanford undergrad majoring in psychology. She also wanted to expand on her prior work as a research assistant for political scientist Shanto Iyengar in his Political Communication Lab, where she studied the effects of negative political campaign ads.

For her research project, Galperin examined the role of social media in inflating Gen Z’s hostility toward people from the opposing political party, a phenomenon political scientists call “affective polarization.”.

“We thought Gen Z would be more polarized and misinformed because we get so much of our news on social media compared to older generations,” Galperin said.

What she and her classmates found reveals a more complicated picture.

While Gen Z respondents who said they used social media daily or almost daily were more likely to dislike the opposing party, their scores were almost identical to those of other generations.

“We found that greater social media engagement is generally linked to more polarized views of political parties, and the effect is seen at similar rates across all generations, not just Gen Z,” noted Galperin, who will be interning with More In Common this summer.

Practices to help campus communities connect across lines of race, faith, ideology, and more.

Galperin also wanted to know whether social media deepens the divide between what Gen Z thinks people from the other side believe versus what they actually think, a phenomenon known as “perception gaps.” In testing people’s perceptions on immigration, she found that Gen Z did not appear to hold wildly distorted views about the other side—findings that push back against the familiar narrative that being online warps a person’s perceptions of politics.

Taken together, actively using social media seems to harden Gen Z’s feelings more than it distorts basic facts.

The class also found a wide range of political viewpoints, including differences between Gen Z who identified as Democrats and Republicans.

For example, in Urogdy’s project, he and his teammates found that those who were the most confident that polarization can be reduced identified as conservatives and Republicans, while liberals and Democrats believed the opposite—a finding that Urogdy noted tracks with prior research: A person’s view of government depends on whether or not their political party is in control.

Galperin’s team also found lower levels of affective polarization among Republicans and Gen Z overall, and Democrats who reported actively using social media daily have higher perception gaps on immigration-related concerns than average.

Industry observers note that another student team’s project revealed further complexities. They found that many Gen Z respondents are more likely than other generations to attribute problems like the affordability crisis to systemic failures in democracy itself rather than to specific policies or leaders. In their data, a notable share of young people said the system itself “is not capable of doing its job,” signaling a deeper, structural disillusionment.

“I think we’re all exhausted by the political system,” Urogdy said. “There’s this underlying feeling that what we want isn’t being translated into tangible change, and I think that there’s this overall feeling that instead of having animosity towards people across the aisle, there’s an animosity towards the system itself.”.

Urogdy is pragmatic about what comes next.

Sources indicate that “We can’t say polarization will disappear if we will it away,” said Urogdy, who is majoring in political science. Now, he feels he has a better understanding of what kinds of solutions matter. If people are disillusioned with the system, surface-level fixes—such as messaging—won’t last, he said. Efforts need to be ongoing. “If Gen Z is still one of the most reachable generations, the answer is sustained civic engagement, where we can rebuild trust in the system while working to reform it. We have a long path ahead,” said Urogdy, who said he is optimistic.

Fabrizio, too, is hopeful. “Gen Z is inheriting a polarized nation, but they are inheriting deep wells of democratic vitality, as well,” Fabrizio remarked. “America has a long history of self-government, a robust civil society, and communities that remain deeply committed to democratic values. Gen Z has high standards for our democracy, but living up to them is within reach. I hope older generations will listen and be inspired by Gen Z’s vision for the American dream.”.

Sources indicate that this article was originally published on Stanford News. Read the original article.

Melissa De Witte is the deputy director for social science communications for the Stanford News Service. She attained an M.A. in Media, Culture, & Communication from NYU and a B.Sc. in Sociology from LSE. She was previously the digital communications manager for the Division of Social Sciences at UC Santa Cruz.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Costco membership is like a real-life, grown-up golden ticket, your passport to bulk-buy deals and steals, as well as its incomparable food court, including the hands-down best menu item, the hot dog and soda combo. It's a terrific shopping option, especially when you have a large family or you're shopping to feed a lot of mouths, as for a party or holiday gathering. While Costco does want to encourage its shoppers to come into its stores and take a look around (and perhaps buy a few things off-the-cuff), the major warehouse chain has also partnered with third-party shopping apps to offer same-day delivery of its goods. But it might not be the best option when you need your Costco fix.

Starting in 2017 with limited availability through Instacart, and now expanding to almost the entire country in 2026 with Uber Eats and DoorDash, Costco's delivery definitely has its positives, but the program isn't without its pitfalls, too. From higher prices to unpredictable delivery times, we're going to highlight several reasons you should maybe think twice before having Costco groceries delivered so that you can weigh your options and make the best decision for yourself.

According to recent reports, while Costco's delivery option does allow nonmembers to shop at the warehouse, the tech giant charges higher prices for most items ordered through the apps, helping offset delivery-related costs. And then there is the actual cost of the deliveries themselves, service fees, plus tips for the drivers, to the point where you might pay as much as 30% to 40% more than if you just shopped in-store.

Sources indicate that if you've ever ordered takeout through DoorDash or Uber Eats, or groceries through Instacart, you might have found that the actual delivery took place long after the original drop-off time you were quoted. And the same thing can happen with Costco same-day delivery, which is a major pitfall if you have organization coming over by a certain time and you need to prepare dinner or snacks.

When you are particular about your produce or search through packages of meat until you find just the right size and price, you might want to think twice about having your Costco order delivered. That's because you have to surrender nearly all control over what goes into your cart (though you can leave notes and instructions for your shoppers), and some shoppers are more careful, considerate, and, well, competent than others.

Recent findings suggest that most items that are available in stores will be visible and available for purchase through apps like Instacart and Uber Eats for same-day delivery. But it's worth noting that Costco also offers two-day delivery, and you may find favorite items missing from its selection. Redditors theorize this may be because the two-day delivery items are sourced from Costco Business Centers, which carry slightly different products.

Finally, Costco also delivers large appliances, so if you're weighing the pros and cons of buying a refrigerator through the warehouse chain, just know that some customers on Reddit have reported miscommunication, sometimes over information as basic as the delivery date, with one user even calling the experience "a nightmare.".

#229720. The Overlooked Ways Love Shows Up in Urban Spaces

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1118 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Berkeley ↗ Open Full Page

The Overlooked Ways Love Shows Up in Urban Spaces

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1118 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Berkeley

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that over the past two decades, my doctoral students and I have focused on studying love, care, kindness, and compassion in urban settings.
  • Sources indicate that but, as someone who has lived and worked in large urban centers—Fresh York City, Chicago, Detroit, Istanbul—I know firsthand that urban centers are also sites of human virtue.
  • My former students and I have been eager to understand how love, generosity, and care manifest and operate in the hyperdiverse, densely populated, loud, fast-paced complexities of urban spaces.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that over the past two decades, my doctoral students and I have focused on studying love, care, kindness, and compassion in urban settings. Why? Because social science research on life in America’s cities is desperately incomplete. Much like the vision of urban life that permeates most of American popular culture, social science research imagines urban areas as sites of overwhelmedness, disengagement, social and moral crisis, threat, and violence.

Sources indicate that but, as someone who has lived and worked in large urban centers—Fresh York City, Chicago, Detroit, Istanbul—I know firsthand that urban centers are also sites of human virtue. People in urban contexts, including those living in high-stress, oversurveilled, underresourced communities, draw daily from deep wells of love, compassion, empathy, kindness, and generosity in the service of caring for each other. From holding doors open for one another, to offering seats on buses and trains, to stopping to help with directions, to paying unexpected compliments, city-dwellers create environments that are saturated with powerful but easily missed acts of care.

My former students and I have been eager to understand how love, generosity, and care manifest and operate in the hyperdiverse, densely populated, loud, fast-paced complexities of urban spaces. Through surveys and interviews, we have sought to understand how adults residing in big cities define love, how they see love being expressed, and their views of the cascading effects of giving and receiving care, generosity, and love.

We have learned that the decision to express love and care for others in large cities is not simply a moral or emotional decision. We offer two examples of the lens needed to notice the presence of love in cities.

First, we have learned that identities matter in experiences of compassion, love, and care between strangers. Urban dwellers’ identity (for example, race or gender), lived experience, context, familial, cultural, and legal systems’ realities work together to shape decisions about whether to extend acts of love to people you do not know. For example, Kehinde, a 26-year-old African American man living in a large, densely populated city, described his experience of giving and receiving kindness, care, and love in his city as shaped by how he navigates other people seeing him as a Black man.

“I will see folks all the time that may need a hand with their bags or crossing the street or just little things like that. And I take a second, hesitate,” Kehinde says. “I don’t want to scare them. I don’t want to come off as a threat.”.

It has been revealed that to get through these moments, Kehinde describes engaging in a practice of analysis and shape-shifting. Before he steps in to offer help, he assesses the environment and changes the way he carries himself so that people will perceive him as a possible helper rather than as a threat. He notes: “I smile a lot more. My voice might change a bit.” He might shrink his body and keep his head down, to avoid seeming intimidating. After helping someone, he moves along without lingering. Reflecting, he acknowledges not being his full, true self in these interactions. “I have to realize I’ve been socialized—made to believe that this is what I need to do in order to navigate the situation.” Kehinde’s story highlights the point that identities matter in economies of care. The images and stereotypes that we construct about people come at a cost even in moments of compassion. Stereotypes affect who we perceive as deserving of care, concern, and protection. Stereotypes also inform our expectations about who can be trusted to help. Stereotyping is not unique to urban settings. But because urban settings tend to be especially diverse spaces, they create abundant opportunities to study how identities and the social scripts we hold affect the way that strangers care for each other across lines of difference. What Kehinde and others bring to the fore is the reality that the targets of stereotyping are aware of the ways that they are perceived. They learn that to be seen as helpful rather than as threatening, they need to read situations correctly, make adjustments to their approaches (e.g., keep “appropriate” distance), and exit situations strategically. Targets of stereotyping must strike a balance between their own deep-seated motivations to behave caringly and their desire to stay safe. For individuals like Kehinde, miscalculations can be costly. If, in the effort to behave lovingly and compassionately, someone is misidentified as a threat, that can lead to a range of consequences from being rebuffed and embarrassed to becoming the target of violence, arrest, or death. The end result is that people consciously or unconsciously learn the rules of engagement around helping strangers.

This piece is part of a three-year GGSC project to explore love's role in promoting social well-being, bridging divides, and contributing to a good, meaningful life.

A second lesson that has emerged from studying love in urban settings is that love lives in the built environment of cities. I highlight this lesson in my Positive Psychology in Urban Settings classes. Cities are often saturated with murals, billboards, and symbols that convey messages of love, solidarity, and belonging. As residents move through neighborhood streets, they may encounter signs prominently posted in shop windows or near the entrances of religious institutions that remind them that “Black Lives Matter,” “Love Is Love,” or “Immigrants Are Welcome Here.” People display rainbow flags and national flags from apartment windows, on cars, and in other spaces, declaring both their own identities and pride for and solidarity with those identities. The architecture of urban spaces may also play a role in expressions of love and care. In many urban neighborhoods, porches, stoops, and front steps serve as places of connection and care. Simple greetings (e.g., “Morning, baby!,” “You doing good?”) voiced by neighbors sitting on their steps serve as ways of spatializing love, care, and connection in urban landscapes.

I return here to my initial point. Our studies of urban areas are desperately incomplete and will remain incomplete until we more fully examine how various forms of human goodness—including love and care—flourish in urban settings. Likewise, our understandings of love and care will remain underdeveloped until we explore how these experiences emerge in the most densely populated, diverse, complex social structures in which people live. We will truly understand love when we understand how it is titrated through place, context, history, culture, religion, structures of power, identities, and a host of individual and relational factors. Urban centers give us powerful opportunities to know love.

Industry observers note that jacqueline Mattis, Ph.D., is dean of the School of Arts and Sciences at Rutgers University-Newark. She studies human goodness in urban contexts.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Trusting others is linked to greater happiness and life satisfaction, a review involving over 2.5 million people finds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.

A review involving over 2.5 million people links one social outlook to greater happiness—and the connection runs both ways.

Trusting others is linked to greater happiness and life satisfaction, a review involving over 2.5 million people finds.

Happier people also tend to become more trusting over time.

The link between trust and happiness is slightly stronger in children, adolescents and older adults, possibly because supportive relationships are especially important at these ages.

Trust may help meet the need to belong by making it easier to build relationships in which people feel supported and secure.

The research combined almost 1,000 findings from studies involving people aged six to 84.

The analysis examined how trust related to everyday emotions, including happiness and sadness, as well as people’s overall satisfaction with their lives.

Greater trust was consistently associated with better wellbeing.

The association was somewhat stronger among children and adolescents than among young and middle-aged adults, and stronger among older adults than young adults.

Trust may matter more at ages when people are building close relationships or becoming more dependent on others.

For younger people, learning whom to trust is part of building meaningful friendships and supportive social networks.

In later life, people may prioritise a smaller circle of close relationships and depend more on others for support.

The researchers distinguished between trust in familiar people, trust in people generally and trust in institutions.

The first involves confidence in someone known personally, such as a partner, friend or relative.

General trust involves expectations about people more broadly, including strangers, while institutional trust concerns organisations such as governments, banks and the police.

All three were associated with better wellbeing, but trust in familiar people showed the strongest connection.

Trust may support wellbeing partly because close relationships require a willingness to be vulnerable.

Expecting someone to respond with care can make it easier to seek help, cooperate and maintain a supportive connection.

These relationships may satisfy the basic psychological need to feel connected to others and cared for in return.

Trust could also provide a broader sense of security and predictability, making the social world feel more dependable.

This may help explain why trust was slightly more closely related to overall life satisfaction than to positive or negative emotions.

Life satisfaction reflects a broader assessment of how life is going, whereas emotions can fluctuate with immediate experiences.

The relationship also worked in the other direction, with greater wellbeing predicting more trust later.

One proposed explanation is that emotions influence how people interpret the world around them.

Feeling happy may encourage more positive perceptions of other people, while anxiety may draw attention towards threats and uncertainty.

Trust and wellbeing could therefore reinforce each other, with supportive expectations helping people feel better and positive feelings making trust easier.

The wider social environment mattered too, with a stronger connection between trust and wellbeing in countries where people were generally more trusting.

A trusting outlook may be more beneficial when the people around us are dependable.

Simply encouraging someone to trust more overlooks the behaviour of the people and institutions receiving that trust.

Professor Catrin Finkenauer, study co-author, remarked:.

“But trust can’t be forced—it has to be earned.”.

The findings therefore highlight the importance of honesty, reliability, transparency and fair treatment in relationships and institutions.

“When we build trust, we also support mental health and stronger communities.”.

The study was published in the journal Psychological Bulletin (Bi et al., 2025).

  • Pierogi are European-style dumplings that you can stuff with everything from chicken to sauerkraut.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Potatoes are almost as key to beef stew as the meat itself. But when you substitute them with pierogi, you aren't necessarily removing the tuber so much as transforming its shape and making it 100% more delicious with a variety of other fillings.

Pierogi are European-style dumplings that you can stuff with everything from chicken to sauerkraut. Still, potato-based fillings are by far the most common, thanks to the delicious combination of a tender wrapping and rich, buttery center that freezes quite well. Making a sort of dumpling soup is one of the best ways to upgrade frozen pierogi, suffusing the dough with an incredibly savory beefiness that's almost impossible to replicate. But it also levels up your stew because you're essentially adding little pockets of mashed potatoes that won't dissipate into the broth!

In a recent development, this is an especially fantastic trick if you don't have much meat to begin with, bulking up your stew quite inexpensively. It's also a way to add ingredients that may not usually make their way into your recipe. Melting cheese directly into the pot may mess up the texture, but contained quantities of cheesy potatoes taste amazing when paired with an umami- and herb-rich broth. The best frozen pierogi brands also come with plenty of their own seasoning, so while bites of the dumplings will have an intense flavor, they won't overseason your stew directly unless you boil them so long that the wrapping breaks.

Beef stew typically needs to cook for at least a couple of hours to develop flavors and tenderize the ingredients. If you add pierogi right away, you run the risk of overboiling the dumplings and making them fall apart. Whether you drop them into the pot to let the wrappings absorb flavor or prepare them separately, timing is critical to preserving their texture.

If you initiative on adding pierogi directly to the stew, it's best to leave them frozen. This allows the wrapping to absorb flavorful broth as the filling thaws. In a pot already at a simmer, 10 minutes should be all you need to ensure everything is heated through. If you use mini versions instead of full-size ones, you may want to cut this down to five minutes — when in doubt, follow package instructions. You can always add a lid and let the residual heat warm them through, but these are much easier to overcook.

Pan-frying pierogi first, then using them as a topping, can be a great way to add a more diverse range of flavors. Properly browned dough not only has a great depth of flavor, but also tends to stand up better against liquids and won't become soggy as quickly. This is especially good for leftovers since you can store your stew and dumplings separately so they won't become oversaturated in the fridge. Frying them up in butter can also add a bit of needed fat if you use a particularly lean cut of meat, making your stew richer.
